## 1. What was read

**908 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster, filtered to `journal article` and excluding reviews, editorials, news, comment and case reports.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 412 | 138 | 81 | 254 | 23 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: cancer -28%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months — queried directly, PubMed returns zero *Nucleic Acids Research* research articles dated 2025-12, and zero *Bioinformatics* in 2024-04, 2025-01, 2025-04 and 2026-03. Those holes are in the source and are reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest, so a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 123, Science 97, Nucleic Acids Res 96, Bioinformatics 53, JAMA 47, Cell 35.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**scGPT and scFoundation arrive in the same journal in the same month — and so
does their audit.** [38409223](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38409223/) (scGPT) and [38844628](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38844628/) (a large-scale
single-cell transcriptomics foundation model) are published in *Nature Methods*
in August 2024, alongside [38528186](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38528186/), which assesses GPT-4 for cell-type
annotation. This is the finding that most changes how the rest of the corpus
should be read. Its November 2025 briefing claimed the virtual-cell vocabulary
had just arrived and that scepticism led it by about three months; the 2025
backfill corrected that to "co-present since spring 2025". The correct statement
is stronger and simpler: **the models and their critics have been in the same
journal in the same month since the models existed.** There was never a lag to
measure.

**The audit reaches the model's own confidence.** [39115813](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39115813/): benchmarking
AlphaFold2's accuracy self-estimates against independent model-quality measures.
Not the prediction — the prediction's stated confidence.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[39121849](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39121849/) (*Cell*) is a support rather than a refutation and is filed as
one: blockade of LAG-3 and PD-1 co-expresses cytotoxic and exhaustion modules in
CD8 T cells. It is here because it is the last month in 2024 in which a
next-generation checkpoint appears in a top-tier general journal with a
mechanistic result attached.

### (b) Method credibility

[39152456](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39152456/) and [39123269](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39123269/) (*Genome Biol*) benchmark single-cell
chromatin analysis and spatial transcriptomics clustering, alignment and
integration. Two benchmarks of two modalities in one journal in one month. The
`method-credibility` thread's real content in 2024 is this: the genre is
established, monthly, and concentrated in two journals. What changes later is
volume, and — measured under one consistent rule for the first time on
2026-08-26 — that change happens in 2026, not in 2025 as this corpus recorded.
